I use a lot of rebar with my forge as it is dirt cheap or if you work at it you can get it for nothing.

One of the thing that I have done (and it made me a ton of money) is build wrought Iron fencing.

What you do is use 1/2 rebar (that stuff is dirt cheap at home depot or lows). Cut it to four foot lengths then hammer weld three lengths of rebar together and Flatten until it is about 3/8 inch thick. Also hammer weld it into 6 foot strips. Now you use a square drift to punch square 3/8 inch hole every 4 or 6 inches along the length

Now you use a square channel strake to make the rebar into square pieces. Now you have a special strake that you have made that fits into the anvil. This strake has a 3/8's inch hole in a horizontal plane. Maker your self a two handed flat piece of metal. Place a square 3/8ths inch hole in the middle of it. Heat your square stock in the forge until it is cherry red. Fit the square end in the strake and place your handle on the other end allowing 2 inches of square stock to stick through the handle. Start rotating the handle and you will put a spiral twist in the square stock. Since the forge is only two fee long you now have to heat the other end and twist that in the same direction or if you want to be ARTSY twist the other direction. Once you have made enough vertical pieces place them in the flat strips you made. Leave the two inches of square stock sticking out of the upper piece. Now you make a bunch of spade shaped points that you weld to the top of the square stock.

Last place a flat piece of stock on each end. weld some small curved hooks on the side and bottom of the flat pieces.

When you assembel your fence you use regular construction brick to make a short foot and a half high wall. Place the hooked ends between to top layer of bricks and mortar it in. Build a 1 foot square tower to fit each end of the wrought iron fence piece and mortar the hooks into the brick.

PAINT THE ALL THE METAL FLAT BLACK WITH RUSTOLEUM PAINT. This makes a wrought iron fence about 6 feet high with spear points on the top to keep people from climbing over it.

Over the years I have made a ton of these fences. They look classy and add to the value of any property.
